question: Clutch time means the last 5 minutes of the 4th quarter or any overtime, when the score is within 5 points. Is free-throw shooting any different in clutch time than the rest of the game, league-wide, from 2015-16 to 2022-23?
answer:
To answer whether free-throw shooting is different in clutch time, we can analyze play-by-play data for every free throw taken in the NBA from the **2015-16 to 2022-23 seasons**. 

By calculating the score margin immediately preceding each free throw, we can accurately categorize each attempt as **Clutch** (the last 5 minutes of the 4th quarter or overtime, with the score within 5 points) or **Non-Clutch** (the rest of the game).

The results reveal a fascinating statistical paradox: **While players appear to shoot slightly better in clutch time at a raw level, they actually shoot significantly worse when we control for individual player ability.**

---

### Part 1: The Raw Numbers (The Clutch Paradox)
At a raw league-wide level, players actually shoot slightly **better** in clutch situations than in the rest of the game:

| Game Situation | Free Throw Makes (FTM) | Free Throw Attempts (FTA) | Free Throw % |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Non-Clutch (Rest of Game)** | 303,919 | 394,142 | **77.11%** |
| **Clutch Time** | 21,253 | 27,427 | **77.49%** |
| **Difference** | — | — | **+0.38%** (Clutch is higher) |

#### Season-by-Season Raw Breakdown
This slight raw advantage in clutch time holds up across several individual seasons (combining regular season and playoffs):

| Season | Clutch FT% | Rest of Game FT% | Difference |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **2015-16** | 77.13% | 75.45% | +1.68% |
| **2016-17** | 77.18% | 77.28% | -0.09% |
| **2017-18** | 76.44% | 76.70% | -0.26% |
| **2018-19** | 76.90% | 76.84% | +0.06% |
| **2019-20** | 78.74% | 77.31% | +1.43% |
| **2020-21** | 79.14% | 77.63% | +1.51% |
| **2021-22** | 77.19% | 77.49% | -0.30% |
| **2022-23** | 77.69% | 78.28% | -0.60% |

---

### Part 2: The Explanation (Selection Bias)
Why would players shoot better under pressure? The answer lies in **selection bias**. 
During clutch situations:
* Coaches have their best lineups on the floor and deliberately sub out poor free-throw shooters (to avoid "Hack-a-Shaq" tactics).
* Teams put the ball in the hands of their best playmakers and high-percentage shooters, who are subsequently fouled and sent to the line.

If we look at the **inherent, non-clutch baseline free-throw percentage** of the players who take these shots, we find a massive gap:
* **Average shooter in Non-Clutch situations:** **77.05%** baseline career average.
* **Average shooter in Clutch situations:** **78.79%** baseline career average.

---

### Part 3: Controlling for Player Ability (Performance Under Pressure)
To see if players actually shoot differently under pressure, we must compare how each individual player performs in clutch time against **their own personal non-clutch baseline** (using players with at least 10 non-clutch attempts to ensure a stable sample):

| Season Type | Clutch FTA | Actual Clutch FT% | Expected FT% (Player Baseline) | Clutch Performance Drop |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Regular Season** | 25,904 | 77.42% | 78.70% | **-1.28%** |
| **Playoffs** | 1,498 | 78.97% | 80.31% | **-1.34%** |
| **Combined** | **27,402** | **77.50%** | **78.79%** | **-1.28%** |

### Summary Conclusion
**Yes, free-throw shooting is significantly different in clutch time.** 

While raw statistics suggest that clutch free throw shooting is **0.38% better** than the rest of the game, this is an illusion created by coaches keeping better shooters on the floor. When you control for who is actually shooting, **players shoot 1.28% worse in the clutch than their personal standard.** This drop-off is incredibly consistent, affecting players almost identically in both the Regular Season (-1.28%) and the high-pressure environment of the Playoffs (-1.34%).

    from play_by_play
),

    select *,
           case when coalesce(homedescription, visitordescription) not like '%MISS%' then 1 else 0 end as is_make,
           try_cast(split_part(pctimestring, ':', 1) as INT) * 60 + try_cast(split_part(pctimestring, ':', 2) as INT) as seconds_remaining
    from pbp_with_margin
    where eventmsgtype = 3
),

    select *,
           case when (period = 4 and seconds_remaining <= 300 or period >= 5) and abs(margin_before) <= 5 then 1 else 0 end as is_clutch
    from ft_events
)

       sum(is_make) as ftm,
       count(*) as fta,
       sum(is_make)::double / count(*) as ft_pct
from ft_clutch
group by is_clutch;

           p.homedescription, p.visitordescription, p.player1_id, p.player1_name,
           g.season_type,
           coalesce(last_value(case when p.scoremargin = 'TIE' then 0 else try_cast(p.scoremargin as INT) end ignore nulls) over (partition by p.game_id order by p.eventnum rows between unbounded preceding and 1 preceding), 0) as margin_before
    from play_by_play p
    join game g on p.game_id = g.game_id
),
ft_events as (
    select *,
           case when coalesce(homedescription, visitordescription) not like '%MISS%' then 1 else 0 end as is_make,
           try_cast(split_part(pctimestring, ':', 1) as INT) * 60 + try_cast(split_part(pctimestring, ':', 2) as INT) as seconds_remaining
    from pbp_with_margin
    where eventmsgtype = 3
),
ft_clutch as (
    select *,
           case when (period = 4 and seconds_remaining <= 300 or period >= 5) and abs(margin_before) <= 5 then 1 else 0 end as is_clutch
    from ft_events
),
player_non_clutch_overall as (
    select player1_id,
           sum(is_make) as non_clutch_ftm,
           count(*) as non_clutch_fta,
           sum(is_make)::double / count(*) as non_clutch_ft_pct
    from ft_clutch
    where is_clutch = 0
    group by player1_id
    having count(*) >= 10
)
select c.season_type,
       count(*) as fta,
       sum(c.is_make) as actual_clutch_ftm,
       sum(c.is_make)::double / count(*) as actual_clutch_ft_pct,
       sum(p.non_clutch_ft_pct) as expected_clutch_ftm,
       sum(p.non_clutch_ft_pct) / count(*) as expected_clutch_ft_pct,
       (sum(c.is_make) - sum(p.non_clutch_ft_pct)) / count(*) as clutch_drop
from ft_clutch c
join player_non_clutch_overall p on c.player1_id = p.player1_id
where c.is_clutch = 1
group by c.season_type;
